subject: Overriding input values if radioButtons is selected

messages.author: b949e0841d7e094b
messages.subject: Overriding input values if radioButtons is selected
parts:
I have a simulation app with several sliders where the user can select parameter values. I'd like to also have a set of predefined parameter values that the user could use as "demos".  Say, something like this in ui.R:

      sliderInput('p', "Parameter:", min = 0, max = 1, value = 0, step = 0.1)
      ,
      checkboxInput("demosPanel", 'label' = "Demos:", 'value' = FALSE)
      ,
      conditionalPanel(
        condition = 'input["demosPanel"]'
        ,
        radioButtons(
          'demosSelected'
          , ''
          , 'choices' = c('Demo 1' = 'demo1', 'Demo 2' = "demo2", 'Demo 3' = 'demo3')
          , 'selected' = 'Demo 1'
        )
      )

I tried to have something like this in server.R

    demosReactive <- reactive({
      if(input$demosSelected=='demo1'){
        input$p = 0.5
      }
    })

but that gives me an error: "Attempted to assign value to a read-only reactivevalues object"

I thought of perhaps wrapping the sliderInput inside a conditionalPanel and tweaking it in a way that only one of the conditionalPanels can be active at a time, but I thought I'd ask before embarking on another venture.

What would be the way to do this? or something like this?

Thanks!

messages.author: 129e07bdb789652f
messages.subject: Re: Overriding input values if radioButtons is selected
parts:
Hi, 

Indeed, you cannot assign a value to an input object as if it was an ordinary R object (http://stla.github.io/ShinyPresentationIntroductory/#5)

Note that the body of reactive({}) in your code does not return anything. That makes no sense because reactive({}) generates a reactive conductor (http://stla.github.io/ShinyPresentationIntroductory/#16). You should use observe({}) in such a situation.

If you only want to update the value of the slider, not the min and the max, the easiest way is to use updateSliderInput().Thus you should replace your wrong reactive conductor with something like:

    observe({
      if(input$demosSelected=='demo1'){
        updateSliderInput("p",0.5)
      }
    })

See the help of updateSliderInput(), I'm not sure of this syntax.

I have made a "demo" app intended to help me (& others?) learn how to use the sliderInput() and updateSliderInput() functions.

It's almost working, but there's a small glitch, namely the app gets (unintentionally) initialized with the values of updateSliderInput() in server.R rather than the values of sliderInput() in ui.R. I'm puzzled because I set 'value' to FALSE around the conditionalPanel against which I have conditioned updateSliderInput, so I didn't expect updateSliderInput() to be called at all at the launch.

I welcome any suggestions on how to fix this. Thanks!

The demo app is here:
http://spark.rstudio.com/toche/demo-plot-function/
http://spark.rstudio.com/toche/demo-plot-function/ui.R
http://spark.rstudio.com/toche/demo-plot-function/server.R

You can go straight to the ui.R and server.R to see the source or read my executive summary below:

I have a sliderInput() in ui.R that is initialized at the values (-5,5), but the app actually gets started at (-2,2), the values in 'demo1' below:

sliderInput(c('X1','X2'), "Range:", min = -10, max = 10, value = c(-5,5), step = 1)

Then I have set up updateSliderInput() in server.R this way:

    observe({
      if (input$demosSelected==0) {return(NULL)} # just in case
      if (input$demosSelected=='demo1'){
       updateSliderInput(session, c('X1','X2'), 'value' = c('-2','2'))
      }
    })

where input$demosSelected and 'demo1' are defined in ui.R as follows:

checkboxInput("demosPanel", 'label' = "Demos:", 'value' = FALSE)
      ,
      conditionalPanel(
        condition = 'input["demosPanel"]'
        ,
        radioButtons(
          'demosSelected'
          , ''
          , 'choices' = c('Demo 1' = 'demo1', 'Demo 2' = "demo2", 'Demo 3' = 'demo3')
          , 'selected' = 'Demo 1'
        )
      )
